provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Long vowel words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify long vowel words.
The pupils should be able to spell long vowel words correctly.
Introduction:
We have learned about short vowel sounds. Today we learn about long vowel sounds.
Long vowel words say their name like in cake.
Content:
Long vowel words have a silent e at the end. The e makes the first vowel say its name.
Examples: cake, kite, rope, tube.
In cake, the a says its name because of the silent e.
In kite, the i says its name because of the silent e.
Class activity:
Pupils will read long vowel words from flashcards.
Pupils will make sentences using long vowel words.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does the a make in cake?
Spell a word with a long vowel sound.
Can you name another long vowel word?
Summary:
Long vowel words have a silent e at the end that makes the first vowel say its name.

topics.title: Two letter blends
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify two letter blends.
The pupils should be able to read words with two letter blends.
Introduction:
We have learned about single letter sounds. Today we learn about two letter blends.
Blends are two letters you hear together.
Content:
Two letter blends are two consonants that make a sound together.
Examples: bl, cr, st, fl.
The word blue starts with bl blend.
The word cry starts with cr blend.
The word stop starts with st blend.
The word fly starts with fl blend.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice saying blend sounds.
Pupils will read words with blends from the board.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does the blend bl make?
Can you name a word that starts with st?
How many letters are in a blend?
Summary:
Two letter blends are two consonants that make a sound together.

topics.title: Comprehension: the farm
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read a passage about the farm.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about the farm passage.
Introduction:
We have learned about animals. Today we read about animals on the farm.
Farms have many animals that help us.
Content:
The farm has many animals.
The cow gives us milk.
The hen lays eggs.
The farmer works hard on the farm.
The farm grows food for us to eat.
Class activity:
Pupils will take turns reading the passage.
Pupils will draw their favorite farm animal.
Evaluation questions:
What animal gives us milk?
What does the hen do?
Who works on the farm?
Summary:
Farms have animals that give us food and other useful things.

topics.title: Grammar: describing words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify describing words.
The pupils should be able to use describing words in sentences.
Introduction:
We have learned about naming words. Today we learn about describing words.
Describing words tell us more about naming words.
Content:
Describing words tell us what something is like.
Examples: red, tall, big, small.
A red car is a car that is red.
A tall boy is a boy that is tall.
We use describing words to make our sentences more interesting.
Class activity:
Pupils will describe objects in the classroom.
Pupils will make sentences using describing words.
Evaluation questions:
What is a describing word?
Describe the color of the board.
Can you use describing words for a book?
Summary:
Describing words tell us more about naming words.

topics.title: Grammar: has and have
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use has correctly in sentences.
The pupils should be able to use have correctly in sentences.
Introduction:
We have learned about naming words. Today we learn about has and have.
Has and have tell us about things we own.
Content:
We use has for one person or thing.
Examples: He has a ball. She has a book.
We use have for more than one person or thing.
Examples: We have books. They have balls.
Remember: I have, you have, we have, they have.
He has, she has, it has.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice making sentences with has and have.
Pupils will fill in the blanks with has or have.
Evaluation questions:
Do we use has for one person or many?
Fill in the blank: He ___ a pencil.
Fill in the blank: They ___ books.
Summary:
We use has for one person or thing and have for more than one.

topics.title: Vocabulary: word building
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add s to words to make them plural.
The pupils should be able to add ing to words to show action.
Introduction:
We have learned about simple words. Today we learn to build new words.
We can add letters to make new words.
Content:
We can add s to a word to show there is more than one.
Example: book becomes books.
We can add ing to a word to show action happening now.
Example: play becomes playing.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice adding s and ing to words.
Pupils will make sentences with new words.
Evaluation questions:
What do we add to show more than one?
What does adding ing to a word show?
Change book to show more than one.
Summary:
We can add s or ing to words to make new words.

topics.title: Composition: my friend
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write three sentences about their friend.
The pupils should be able to read their composition aloud.
Introduction:
We have learned to describe things. Today we write about our friend.
Friends are special people in our lives.
Content:
When writing about your friend, think about:
What is your friend's name?
What does your friend like to do?
Why do you like your friend?
Write three simple sentences about your friend.
Example: My friend is Ada. Ada likes to play. Ada is kind.
Class activity:
Pupils will write three sentences about their friend.
Pupils will take turns reading their composition aloud.
Evaluation questions:
How many sentences should you write?
What should you write about your friend?
Why are friends special?
Summary:
We can write three simple sentences to describe our friend.

topics.title: Letter writing: greeting a friend
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write a greeting in a letter.
The pupils should be able to write a closing in a letter.
Introduction:
We have learned to write sentences. Today we learn to write letters.
Letters are how we talk to friends who are far away.
Content:
A friendly letter has parts:
Greeting: Dear Friend,
Body: Write what you want to say.
Closing: From your name.
Example:
Dear Amina,
I hope you are well. I miss you.
From Ada
Class activity:
Pupils will write a simple friendly letter to a friend.
Pupils will practice writing greetings and closings.
Evaluation questions:
What do you write at the start of a letter?
What do you write at the end of a letter?
Who do you write letters to?
Summary:
A friendly letter has a greeting, body and closing.

topics.title: Spelling and dictation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to spell words correctly.
The pupils should be able to write words from dictation.
Introduction:
We have learned many words. Today we practice spelling them.
Spelling means writing words correctly.
Content:
To spell well, we use look, cover, write, check.
Look at the word carefully.
Cover the word with your hand.
Write the word from memory.
Check if you spelled it right.
We will have a spelling bee where we take turns spelling words.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice spelling words using look, cover, write, check.
The class will have a spelling bee competition.
Evaluation questions:
What are the four steps to spell well?
Can you spell the word friend?
What is a spelling bee?
Summary:
We can use look, cover, write, check to spell words well.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what we learned this year.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about what we learned.
Introduction:
Today we revise all we learned this year and have a quiz.
We will remember the important things we learned.
Content:
We will review:
Long vowel words and two letter blends.
Describing words and has have.
Word building with s and ing.
Writing about friends and letters.
Spelling words correctly.
Class activity:
The teacher will ask questions about what we learned this year.
Pupils will work in teams to answer questions.
Evaluation questions:
What is a describing word?
When do we use has?
What does adding ing to a word do?
Summary:
We have learned many important things in English this year.
